sections.content: Tucked between Milwaukee and Chicago along Lake Michigan's western shore, Kenosha, Wisconsin has quietly earned a reputation as one of the Midwest's most underrated real estate markets. With relatively low entry prices, strong rental demand, and a growing local economy, savvy investors are starting to take notice. Whether you are a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started — check out our guide to [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) for the fundamentals — Kenosha offers a compelling mix of deal types and profit potential. This guide walks you through everything you need to know about finding real estate deals in Kenosha WI, from the best neighborhoods to market trends and tips for out-of-state investors.
Kenosha WI Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Kenosha is Wisconsin's fourth-largest city, with a population of around 100,000 residents. Its location is a major selling point — it sits just 35 miles north of Chicago and 35 miles south of Milwaukee, making it a realistic commuter city for workers in both metro areas. That geography creates steady housing demand. Amazon, Uline, and Snap-on Tools are among the major employers anchoring the local economy, and ongoing infrastructure investment is attracting new businesses to the region. The Kenosha Area Business Alliance reports consistent job growth, which supports both homeownership and rental demand — two critical ingredients for strong real estate returns.

The median home price in Kenosha hovers around $230,000 to $255,000 as of 2024, which is dramatically lower than Chicago's median of roughly $350,000 and even below Milwaukee's average. This price gap makes Kenosha an accessible entry point for investors who want Midwest stability without the steep buy-in costs of larger metros. Days on market typically run 20 to 35 days for move-in-ready homes, while distressed properties can sit longer — creating opportunity for investors willing to move quickly on the right deal.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Deals in Kenosha WI

Not all zip codes are created equal. In Kenosha, the neighborhoods you target will depend heavily on your investment strategy. Here is a breakdown of the areas that consistently attract investor interest:
Downtown Kenosha and the Lakefront District

The downtown corridor along the lakefront has seen significant revitalization over the past decade. Historic homes in this area, many of them older Victorians and bungalows, appeal to buyers and renters who want walkability and character. Values here are climbing, which makes this zone ideal for fix-and-flip investors who can purchase distressed properties before prices climb further. ARVs on renovated homes in the lakefront district can reach $300,000 to $380,000 depending on condition and finishes.
Uptown and Central Kenosha

Uptown Kenosha is a bread-and-butter neighborhood for wholesalers and buy-and-hold investors. Median prices here sit between $150,000 and $200,000, and single-family rentals can generate monthly rents of $1,100 to $1,500. The neighborhood has a mix of blue-collar homeowners and renters, creating both wholesale deal flow and stable tenant demand. Motivated sellers — particularly aging homeowners and absentee landlords — are more common here than in pricier suburbs.
Pleasant Prairie and Somers (Suburban Growth)

For investors targeting higher-end flips or long-term appreciation plays, the suburban townships of Pleasant Prairie and Somers offer newer construction and stronger school ratings. Homes here range from $280,000 to $450,000. While margins are tighter on flips, rental demand from corporate tenants and commuters makes this zone attractive for cash-flow-focused landlords.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Kenosha
Wholesale Deals

Kenosha's mix of aging housing stock and motivated sellers creates a steady pipeline for wholesalers. Probate properties, pre-foreclosures, and tired landlords are common deal sources. The key is finding off-market opportunities before they hit the MLS. Learn more about sourcing these types of deals in our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals). Assignment fees in Kenosha typically range from $8,000 to $20,000 depending on the deal. If you are new to the strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide is a great starting point.
Fix-and-Flip Opportunities

Flippers are finding solid margins in Kenosha, particularly in the downtown and Uptown zones. A typical deal might involve purchasing a distressed 3-bedroom bungalow for $120,000, investing $45,000 in renovations, and selling at an ARV of $210,000 — netting a gross profit of around $45,000 before holding costs. Before running with those numbers on any deal, use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to validate your after-repair value estimate based on real comparable sales.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

Kenosha's rental market is driven by a large workforce population, students attending Carthage College and UW-Parkside, and commuters who prefer renting to buying. Gross rental yields on single-family homes in Central Kenosha can hit 8% to 11%, which is well above the national average of around 5% to 6%. Multifamily properties — duplexes and small apartment buildings — are also available in the $200,000 to $400,000 range and tend to attract serious buy-and-hold investors looking for multiple income streams under one roof.

It factors in ARV, repair costs, holding costs, and your target profit margin so you can make confident, data-backed offers in minutes.
Kenosha Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

Several macro and local trends are shaping Kenosha's investment landscape right now. First, rising interest rates have cooled buyer demand slightly, which is actually good news for investors — it means less competition on deals and more motivated sellers who cannot afford to wait for the market to recover. Second, the Chicago migration trend continues to push buyers and renters into Kenosha, as remote and hybrid workers seek lower costs of living without giving up Midwest amenities. Third, Kenosha County has approved several commercial and residential development projects that should increase property values along key corridors over the next three to five years.

items: Median home prices have increased roughly 18% over the past three years, with more modest growth expected in 2024
Rental vacancy rates in Kenosha sit below 5%, signaling strong landlord conditions
Pre-foreclosure filings have ticked up slightly in 2024, creating more wholesale opportunities
New construction is limited relative to demand, which keeps resale values of renovated homes elevated
The I-94 corridor between Kenosha and Chicago continues to attract distribution and logistics employers, supporting job growth

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Kenosha

Kenosha's affordability and proximity to two major metros makes it a logical target for out-of-state investors, but there are real pitfalls to avoid if you are not local. Understanding how to [Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) is essential before deploying capital in any new market, and Kenosha is no exception. Here are the most important considerations:

items: Build a local team first: Find a Kenosha-area real estate attorney, a property manager familiar with Wisconsin landlord-tenant law, and a general contractor who knows local rehab costs before you close your first deal
Understand Wisconsin property taxes: Kenosha County property taxes average 1.8% to 2.2% of assessed value, which is higher than the national average and must be factored into your cash flow analysis
Drive the neighborhoods virtually: Use Google Street View and satellite tools to assess block-by-block conditions, then visit in person before committing to any significant purchase
Target the right seller types: Probate leads, tax-delinquent properties, and absentee-owned homes in Kenosha have produced the most consistent wholesale and flip opportunities for out-of-state buyers
Use local MLS data for comps: National tools often lag behind local reality. Partner with a Kenosha investor-friendly agent who can pull accurate sold comparables quickly
Explore Kenosha-specific deal flow at [aiwholesail.com/markets/kenosha-wi](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/kenosha-wi) to stay current on active opportunities in the market

sections.content: The best real estate markets are not always the most glamorous ones. They are the markets where the numbers work, demand is real, and most investors are still not looking. Kenosha fits that profile right now.

Whether you plan to wholesale your first deal, flip a dated bungalow, or build a portfolio of cash-flowing rentals, Kenosha WI checks the boxes that serious investors look for: affordable entry prices, consistent demand, and room for appreciation. The key is moving with intention — knowing your numbers, building local relationships, and sourcing deals before they hit the open market. Investors who do that groundwork now will be well-positioned as this market continues to mature.
